title: Validation Orchestrator & Upgrade Runbook for LTS/Channel Rollouts
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a reusable Validation Orchestrator and accompanying upgrade runbook to drive safe rollouts across LTS and channel releases. The orchestrator should: (1) select an appropriate test subset based on delta metadata between versions, (2) schedule distributed validation agents close to target capacity (hosted / dedicated / private), (3) run smoke checks, perf fingerprint comparisons, and eval-suite regressions, (4) emit gate decisions to the release-gates service and annotate the Console rollout UI. The runbook documents manual fallbacks and post-rollback steps for Private deployments and KMS/HSM-sensitive upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: Validation Orchestrator prototype can run a release validation job end-to-end for staging and produce a structured gate decision JSON
Orchestrator dynamically picks tests by diff metadata and supports per-customer exclusion lists
Perf fingerprinting job produces <=5% token-latency regression detection and flags anomalies to SLO-alerting
Upgrade runbook for LTS -> minor version upgrades with explicit prechecks for KV cache, quantization, and kernel ABI
Console shows gate state for a rollout and links to the failed test artifacts and reproducible evaluation inputs
updates: 2026-03-10: Spike completed — proof-of-concept harness that runs a smoke + perf-fingerprint pipeline on a single dedicated node. Observed nondeterminism in eval suites due to RNG seed handling.

2026-03-11: Prototype refactor — added deterministic seeding and artifact capture (traces + token timing). Increased perf test warmup to 60s to stabilize throughput measurement. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4782

2026-03-12: Integration — hooked orchestrator to release-metadata service to compute delta-based test selection. Implemented per-channel test profiles (lts-heavy, minor-heavy, patch-smoke). Draft runbook sections authored in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RL/Upgrade+Runbook

2026-03-13: QA request — asking platform QA to run the orchestrator against the dedicated staging pool and Private sandbox (on-prem VM). Noting one flaky eval (semantic-rerank) — cloning test with increased sample size to reduce false positives.
Next steps: add gating thresholds per-customer SLA, implement auto-rollback trigger recipe in release-gates, schedule security review for KMS/HSM interaction under Private upgrades.
notes: Design decisions: prefer small, targeted evals early in pipeline and run full eval suite only if a gate trips. For Private deployments where artifact upload is restricted, orchestrator will stream compressed artifact bundles to customer-managed storage or allow signed temporary upload tokens. Flaky-test mitigation: add deterministic seeds, canonical prompt fixtures, and higher sampling for nondeterministic tests.
implementation_summary: Orchestrator implemented as a Kubernetes job controller in platform repo; agents are lightweight containers that run local traffic replays or synthesized microbenchmarks. Gate evaluation uses a configurable ruleset with hard thresholds (latency/regression) and soft checks (quality A/B delta). Gate decisions are versioned and auditable in release-gates DB. Initial rollout will gate runtime-1.22 release on staging and one internal customer sandbox.
qa_plan: QA to run three validation runs per week on staging and one run against Private sandbox. Capture artifact bundles for any failing gate. Escalation path: on high-impact failure, notify on-call infra and open rollback ticket referencing ENG-23321-runbook
owner_notes: We should coordinate with Platform Security before enabling artifact uploads from Private sandboxes. Coordinate with Solutions Eng to test runbook steps for enterprise upgrade scenarios.
